formulations.label: Cream 1%
formulations.note: No emc SmPC; the UK SPC was taken from the MHRA products site. Contains cetyl alcohol and propylene glycol.

src.q: Contains silver sulfadiazine 1.0%w/w.
Contains 4% w/w cetyl alcohol and 7% w/w propylene glycol.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Prevention and treatment of infection in burn wounds.

src.q: is indicated for the prophylaxis and treatment of infection in burn wounds

items.t: Aid to short-term treatment of infection in leg ulcers and pressure sores; aid to infection prevention in skin graft donor sites and extensive abrasions; conservative management of finger-tip injuries.

src.q: as an aid to the short-term treatment of infection in leg ulcers and pressure sores
skin graft donor sites and extensive abrasions
conservative management of finger- tip injuries

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK SPC (MHRA products) accessed; no emc SmPC, MHRA Drug Safety Update, SPS or BUMPS page specific to silver sulfadiazine was found.

items.t: Burns: clean the wound and apply a 3 to 5 mm layer over all affected areas. Re-apply at least every 24 hours, or more often if there is a lot of exudate.

src.q: applied over all the affected areas to a depth of 3-5mm
should be re-applied at least every 24 hours, or more frequently if the volume of exudate is large

items.t: Leg ulcers and pressure sores: clean and debride, fill the cavity to at least 3 to 5 mm, cover with an absorbent dressing; change daily (every 48 hours may be enough for less exudative wounds). Not recommended for very exudative ulcers.

src.q: The cavity of the ulcer should be filled with FLAMAZINE Cream to a depth of at least 3-5mm.
The dressings should normally be changed daily but for wounds which are less exudative, less frequent changes (every 48 hours) may be acceptable.
is not recommended for use in leg or pressure ulcers that are very exudative

items.t: Finger-tip injuries: achieve haemostasis, apply a 3 to 5 mm layer, change dressings every 2 to 3 days.

src.q: Haemostasis of the injury should be achieved prior to the application
Dressings should be changed every 2-3 days.

items.t: Contraindicated in premature infants and newborns in the first months of life; the SPC states contraindicated in children up to 3 months (risk of kernicterus).

src.q: contraindicated in children aged to three months
on premature infants or on newborn infants during the first months of life

items.t: Pregnancy at or near term, premature infants, and newborns in the first months of life (sulfonamides can cause kernicterus).

src.q: As sulphonamides are known to cause kernicterus, FLAMAZINE Cream should not be used at, or near term pregnancy, on premature infants or on newborn infants during the first months of life.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, silver sulfadiazine, or excipients such as cetyl alcohol or propylene glycol.

src.q: contraindicated in patients known to be hypersensitive to sulphonamides and silver sulfadiazine or to other components of the preparation such as cetyl alcohol or propylene glycol

items.t: Life-threatening skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis) have been reported, highest risk in the first weeks. Warn patients, monitor the skin closely, and stop if signs appear (e.g. spreading rash with blisters or mucosal lesions). Never restart after SJS/TEN.

src.q: Life-threatening cutaneous reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN)) have been reported with the use of silver sulfadiazine.
The highest risk for occurrence of SJS or TEN is within the first weeks of treatment.
silver sulfadiazine must not be re-started in this patient at any time

items.t: Use with caution in significant hepatic or renal impairment.

src.q: should be used with caution in the presence of significant hepatic or renal impairment

items.t: Caution in people sensitive to systemic sulfonamides and in G6PD deficiency.

src.q: Caution of use is required in patients known to be sensitive to systemic sulphonamides and in individuals known to have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.

items.t: May delay separation of burn eschar and change the appearance of burn wounds.

src.q: may delay separation of burn eschar and may alter the appearance of the burn wounds

items.t: Large-area burns: serum sulfadiazine may approach therapeutic levels and alter the effect of systemic medicines, especially oral antidiabetic medicines and phenytoin. Monitor blood levels, as their effects can be potentiated.

src.q: In large-area burns where serum sulfadiazine levels may approach therapeutic levels, it should be noted that the effects of systemically administered drugs may be altered.
This can especially apply to oral hypoglycaemic agents and to phenytoin.
it is recommended that blood levels should be monitored as their effects can be potentiated

items.t: Enzymatic debriding agents: silver may inactivate them; using both may be inappropriate.

src.q: As silver may inactivate enzymatic debriding agents, concomitant use may be inappropriate.

items.t: Povidone-iodine: the povidone-iodine SPCs say silver-containing products and povidone-iodine reduce each other's effect and should not be used together.

src.q: Products containing mercury, silver, hydrogen peroxide, and taurolidine may interact with povidone-iodine and cause mutual reduction of effects.
Povidone-iodine should not be used together with alkali, hydrogen peroxide, taurolidine, tannic acid, and silver and mercury salts.

items.t: Use with caution in significant renal impairment (no numeric threshold given). Sulfadiazine is absorbed through wounds and excreted in the urine; renal failure is a very rare adverse effect.

src.q: should be used with caution in the presence of significant hepatic or renal impairment
Sulfadiazine is excreted in the urine.
Very rare: Renal failure

items.t: Use with caution in significant hepatic impairment (severity not defined).

src.q: should be used with caution in the presence of significant hepatic or renal impairment

items.t: Contraindicated at or near term (kernicterus risk with sulfonamides). No clinical data on exposed pregnancies; animal studies showed no hazard.

src.q: should not be used in pregnant females at term
no clinical data on exposed pregnancies are available, although animal studies have not shown any hazard

items.t: Caution in breastfeeding: absorbed sulfadiazine passes into milk at 15 to 35% of serum levels.

src.q: caution is required in nursing mothers
Systemically absorbed sulfadiazine can be excreted in breast milk although at concentrations 15-35% of those found in serum.

reproductive.note: The UK SPC (MHRA products) gives no fertility or contraception statement.

items.t: Common: leucopenia (3 to 5% of burns patients, often 2 to 3 days after starting; usually self-limiting), application-site burning, itching, application-site rash including eczema and contact dermatitis.

src.q: Leukopenia has been reported in 3-5% of burns patients
often manifests itself 2-3 days after treatment has commenced
Common: Application site burning
Common: Application site rash (including eczema and contact dermatitis)

items.t: Very rare Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis: stop treatment and never restart.

src.q: Very rare: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs) Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN)
silver sulfadiazine treatment should be discontinued

items.t: Very rare renal failure. Rare argyria (silver absorption) with large wounds or prolonged use.

src.q: Very rare: Renal failure
Rare: Argyria
in large area wounds and/or after prolonged application,systemic absorption of silver can occur causing clinical argyria

items.t: If leucopenia occurs, monitor the blood count until it returns to normal (treatment usually need not stop).

src.q: the blood count must be monitored to ensure that it returns to normal within a few days
therapy with FLAMAZINE Cream does not usually need to be discontinued

items.t: Monitor closely for skin reactions, especially in the first weeks.

src.q: Patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions.

items.t: Stop if signs of SJS/TEN appear (e.g. progressive rash with blisters or mucosal lesions).

src.q: If symptoms or signs of SJS or TEN (e.g. progressive skin rash often with blisters or mucosal lesions) are present, silver sulfadiazine treatment should be discontinued.

items.t: Large-area burns: monitor blood levels of oral antidiabetic medicines and phenytoin.

src.q: it is recommended that blood levels should be monitored as their effects can be potentiated

items.t: Apply with a sterile gloved hand and/or sterile spatula. Hand burns: apply and enclose the hand in a clear plastic bag or glove closed at the wrist; encourage movement.

src.q: This application is best achieved with a sterile gloved hand and/or sterile spatula.
the whole hand enclosed in a clear plastic bag or glove, which is then closed at the wrist

items.t: Ulcers: keep the cream off surrounding normal skin, as prolonged contact can macerate it.

src.q: can cause maceration of normal skin on prolonged contact

items.t: One container is for one person only. Discard tubes 7 days after opening and large pots 24 hours after opening.

src.q: The contents of one container are for the treatment of one person.
Tubes of FLAMAZINE Cream should be discarded 7 days after opening.
250g and 500g pots should be discarded 24 hours after opening.

items.t: Report any spreading rash, blisters or mouth/eye sores at once.

src.q: Patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions.
